steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Make sure to disconnect the circuit breaker or power cable before servicing.

steps.title: Inspect motor connectors
steps.body: Check circulation motor connector and startup condenser connector seated.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Check circulation motor connector and startup condenser connector seated.

steps.title: Circulation motor coil
steps.body: Disconnect connector. Measure coil resistance. Normal: approx. 5.8 Ω.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Disconnect connector. Measure coil resistance. Normal: approx. 5.8 Ω.

steps.title: Clear water passages
steps.body: Remove foreign material from water passages and verify nozzles rotate freely.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove foreign material from water passages and verify nozzles rotate freely.

steps.title: Nozzle injects water in Smart Install?
steps.body: Smart Install step 2/3: circulation pump and alternation nozzles spray normally?
steps.sourceExcerpt: Smart Install step 2/3: circulation pump and alternation nozzles spray normally?

steps.title: Replace circulation motor
steps.body: Replace circulation motor when coil open or spray fails after clearing passages.

steps.title: Continue component check
steps.body: Smart Install active. Continue below for component-specific verification.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Manual Mode — component steps per §4-2.

steps.title: Circulation OK
steps.body: Motor and nozzle path verified.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Make sure to disconnect the circuit breaker or power cable before servicing.

steps.title: Inspect CN401 sub comms
steps.body: Check CN401 main-to-sub harness (pins 4–5 TX/RX) and inverter PBA connection.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Check CN401 main-to-sub harness (pins 4–5 TX/RX) and inverter PBA connection.

steps.title: Comms stable in test mode?
steps.body: AC: main↔sub fails 24 s (6 s in test mode). AC6: no inverter response 3 s ×3.
steps.sourceExcerpt: AC: main↔sub fails 24 s (6 s in test mode). AC6: no inverter response 3 s ×3.

steps.title: Sub PBA and inverter seated?
steps.body: Reseat sub PBA and inverter PBA connectors. Check for corrosion or damaged pins.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Reseat sub PBA and inverter PBA connectors. Check for corrosion or damaged pins.

steps.title: Replace sub or inverter PBA
steps.body: Replace failed sub PBA or inverter PBA.

steps.title: Replace main PBA
steps.body: Replace main PBA when harness good but comms fail.

steps.title: Communication OK
steps.body: PBA communication verified.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Make sure to disconnect the circuit breaker or power cable before servicing.

steps.title: Detergent in dispenser?
steps.body: Confirm detergent loaded and dispenser not blocked by large items.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Confirm detergent loaded and dispenser not blocked by large items.

steps.title: Load detergent and clear obstruction
steps.body: Add detergent; rearrange racks so dispenser can open.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Add detergent; rearrange racks so dispenser can open.

steps.title: Inspect dispenser connector
steps.body: Reconnect dispenser connector CN202 pin 5.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Reconnect dispenser connector CN202 pin 5.

steps.title: Dispenser solenoid
steps.body: Disconnect connector. Measure resistance. Normal: approx. 2.3 kΩ.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Disconnect connector. Measure resistance. Normal: approx. 2.3 kΩ.

steps.title: Dispenser operates 130 s in Smart Install?
steps.body: Auto step 3 runs dispenser actuator 130 seconds.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Auto step 3 runs dispenser actuator 130 seconds.

steps.title: Replace dispenser
steps.body: Replace dispenser when solenoid open.

steps.title: Replace main PBA
steps.body: Replace main PBA when 120 V missing at CN101/CN202 during operate.

steps.title: Continue component check
steps.body: Smart Install active. Continue below for component-specific verification.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Manual Mode — component steps per §4-2.

steps.title: Dispenser OK
steps.body: Dispenser circuit verified.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Make sure to disconnect the circuit breaker or power cable before servicing.

steps.title: Inspect distributor motor
steps.body: Check CN202 pin 7 distributor motor connector and cam/vane position.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Check CN202 pin 7 distributor motor connector and cam/vane position.

steps.title: Vane alternates in Smart Install?
steps.body: Step 1 moves vane during drain; step 2/3 alternates nozzle positions. PC if position not detected in 2 min.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Step 1 moves vane during drain; step 2/3 alternates nozzle positions. PC if position not detected in 2 min.

steps.title: Continue component check
steps.body: Smart Install active. Continue below for component-specific verification.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Manual Mode — component steps per §4-2.

steps.title: Cam and vane mechanically correct?
steps.body: Verify cam location correct and vane parks before bottom nozzle spray.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Verify cam location correct and vane parks before bottom nozzle spray.

steps.title: Replace distributor motor
steps.body: Replace distributor motor or synchronous motor when PC persists.

steps.title: Distributor OK
steps.body: Distributor and vane path verified.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Make sure to disconnect the circuit breaker or power cable before servicing.

steps.title: Door closure
steps.body: Verify door latched completely, racks not interfering, unit level.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Verify door latched completely, racks not interfering, unit level.

steps.title: Door switch voltage correct?
steps.body: Blue wire switch: Power On door open 9.5–12.5 V; Power Off door open 5.5–7.0 V; door closed <2 V.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Blue wire switch: Power On door open 9.5–12.5 V; Power Off door open 5.5–7.0 V; door closed <2 V.

steps.title: Reconnect door switch
steps.body: Reconnect door sensing switch connectors on blue wire circuit.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Reconnect door sensing switch connectors on blue wire circuit.

steps.title: Door switch continuity?
steps.body: Power off, connector removed: OPEN when door open; SHORT when door closed.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power off, connector removed: OPEN when door open; SHORT when door closed.

steps.title: Replace door switch
steps.body: Replace door sensing switch when continuity fails.

steps.title: Door switch OK
steps.body: Door circuit verified — if cycle still won't start, replace main PBA.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Make sure to disconnect the circuit breaker or power cable before servicing.

steps.title: Drain path
steps.body: Inspect drain hose, air gap, and filter for obstruction.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Inspect drain hose, air gap, and filter for obstruction.

steps.title: Inspect CN203 drain pump
steps.body: Check CN203 pin 3 AC drain pump connector. Inspect O-ring on pump housing.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Check CN203 pin 3 AC drain pump connector. Inspect O-ring on pump housing.

steps.title: Drain pump runs in Smart Install?
steps.body: Smart Install step 1/4/6: drain pump cycles (14 s on / 2 s off pattern). 5C if pump stuck or not draining.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Smart Install step 1/4/6: drain pump cycles (14 s on / 2 s off pattern). 5C if pump stuck or not draining.

steps.title: Continue component check
steps.body: Smart Install active. Continue below for component-specific verification.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Manual Mode — component steps per §4-2.

steps.title: Clear pump obstruction
steps.body: Remove foreign object from drain pump impeller. Re-test drain.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove foreign object from drain pump impeller. Re-test drain.

steps.title: Replace drain pump
steps.body: Replace drain pump or inverter PBA when pump fails after clearing obstruction.

steps.title: Drain OK
steps.body: Drain pump and path verified.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Make sure to disconnect the circuit breaker or power cable before servicing.

steps.title: Rinse aid sufficient?
steps.body: Rinse refill LED off; dispenser has rinse aid.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Rinse refill LED off; dispenser has rinse aid.

steps.title: Refill rinse aid
steps.body: Fill rinse aid dispenser and retest dry performance.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Fill rinse aid dispenser and retest dry performance.

steps.title: Inspect dry fan and actuator
steps.body: Reconnect dry fan motor and thermal actuator connectors (CN201/CN302).
steps.sourceExcerpt: Reconnect dry fan motor and thermal actuator connectors (CN201/CN302).

steps.title: Dry fan motor coil
steps.body: Disconnect connector. Normal: approx. 150 Ω.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Disconnect connector. Normal: approx. 150 Ω.

steps.title: Thermal actuator
steps.body: Disconnect connector. Normal: approx. 1.45 kΩ.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Disconnect connector. Normal: approx. 1.45 kΩ.

steps.title: Fan and auto door in Smart Install step 5?
steps.body: Step 5: auto door actuator runs; fan 30 s. FC if fan <3000 RPM; dC3 if door not sensed open.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Step 5: auto door actuator runs; fan 30 s. FC if fan <3000 RPM; dC3 if door not sensed open.

steps.title: Replace dry fan
steps.body: Replace dry fan motor assembly.

steps.title: Replace thermal actuator
steps.body: Replace thermal actuator when open.

steps.title: Replace main PBA
steps.body: Replace main PBA when 120 V relay drive missing during dry operate.

steps.title: Continue component check
steps.body: Smart Install active. Continue below for component-specific verification.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Manual Mode — component steps per §4-2.

steps.title: Dry system OK
steps.body: Dry fan and auto door path verified.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Make sure to disconnect the circuit breaker or power cable before servicing.

steps.title: Water supply open and pressure OK?
steps.body: Faucet open; pressure 20–120 psi. Inlet hose and aqua-stop filter clear.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Faucet open; pressure 20–120 psi. Inlet hose and aqua-stop filter clear.

steps.title: Correct water supply
steps.body: Open valve, clear inlet filter/aqua-stop, verify adequate pressure.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Open valve, clear inlet filter/aqua-stop, verify adequate pressure.

steps.title: Inspect CN202 valve
steps.body: Check water valve connector CN202 pin 3 circuit seated; inspect flow meter at CN505 pin 12.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Check water valve connector CN202 pin 3 circuit seated; inspect flow meter at CN505 pin 12.

steps.title: Water fills in Smart Install step 2?
steps.body: Smart Install Auto step 2 supplies 4.5 L. 4C if pulses <10 in 20 s or level not reached in 60 min.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Smart Install Auto step 2 supplies 4.5 L. 4C if pulses <10 in 20 s or level not reached in 60 min.

steps.title: Continue component check
steps.body: Smart Install active. Continue below for component-specific verification.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Manual Mode — component steps per §4-2.

steps.title: Flow meter pulses during fill?
steps.body: Case brake/flow meter detects pulses during fill. 4C5 if 200 pulses detected when valve should be off.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Case brake/flow meter detects pulses during fill. 4C5 if 200 pulses detected when valve should be off.

steps.title: Replace inlet valve
steps.body: Replace water valve when supply good but no fill.

steps.title: Replace flow meter / case brake
steps.body: Replace case brake or flow meter sensor when pulse detection fails.

steps.title: Fill path OK
steps.body: Fill and flow meter verified.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Make sure to disconnect the circuit breaker or power cable before servicing.

steps.title: Hot water supply
steps.body: Verify inlet hose connected to hot water supply. Check water level in tub and drain hose installation.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Verify inlet hose connected to hot water supply. Check water level in tub and drain hose installation.

steps.title: Heater heats in Smart Install step 3?
steps.body: In Smart Install Manual Mode step 3: circulation pump runs 10 s then heater operates. Temperature should rise ≥2°C within 30 s after alternation cycle; HC1 if no rise in 10 min.
steps.sourceExcerpt: In Smart Install Manual Mode step 3: circulation pump runs 10 s then heater operates. Temperature should rise ≥2°C within 30 s after alternation cycle; HC1 if no rise in 10 min.

steps.title: Verify thermistor
steps.body: Run samsungdw-thermistor procedure — faulty thermistor can cause HC/HC1.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Run samsungdw-thermistor procedure — faulty thermistor can cause HC/HC1.

steps.title: Continue component check
steps.body: Smart Install active. Continue below for component-specific verification.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Manual Mode — component steps per §4-2.

steps.title: Heater bracket and connections?
steps.body: Inspect heater nut torqued into bracket-heater, both heater connectors seated, no scale or open at heater terminals.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Inspect heater nut torqued into bracket-heater, both heater connectors seated, no scale or open at heater terminals.

steps.title: Replace heater
steps.body: Replace heater assembly when connections good but no heat in Smart Install.

steps.title: Heater path OK
steps.body: Heater operational — if fault persists, replace main PBA.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Make sure to disconnect the circuit breaker or power cable before servicing.

steps.title: Inspect sub PBA connectors
steps.body: Reconnect sub PBA and touch panel harnesses.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Reconnect sub PBA and touch panel harnesses.

steps.title: LED and key test pass?
steps.body: Hi-Temp+Sanitize+Power → all LEDs. Normal–Sanitize → each LED. Delay Start ×8 cycles LEDs. Start → 1234. Auto → version.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Hi-Temp+Sanitize+Power → all LEDs. Normal–Sanitize → each LED. Delay Start ×8 cycles LEDs. Start → 1234. Auto → version.

steps.title: Stuck button or object on panel?
steps.body: bC2 when button held ≥30 s. Remove object; verify touch panel not damaged.
steps.sourceExcerpt: bC2 when button held ≥30 s. Remove object; verify touch panel not damaged.

steps.title: Replace sub PBA / touch panel
steps.body: Replace sub PBA or touch button PBA when bC2/bC3 or LED test fails.

steps.title: HMI OK
steps.body: Touch panel and sub PBA verified.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Make sure to disconnect the circuit breaker or power cable before servicing.

steps.title: Inspect for water leakage
steps.body: Check shutter and base for water traces. Normal: no leakage trace.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Check shutter and base for water traces. Normal: no leakage trace.

steps.title: Leak sensor reads >3 V after dry?
steps.body: CN505 pin 3 leakage input: LC when ≤3 V for 3 s. After 3 min drain, sensor should read >3 V if dry.
steps.sourceExcerpt: CN505 pin 3 leakage input: LC when ≤3 V for 3 s. After 3 min drain, sensor should read >3 V if dry.

steps.title: Locate and repair leak
steps.body: Find leak at hose, door, sump seals, heater, or pump joints. Repair and dry base.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Find leak at hose, door, sump seals, heater, or pump joints. Repair and dry base.

steps.title: Leak resolved
steps.body: No active leak; sensor dry. Replace main PBA only if leak repaired but LC persists.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Make sure to disconnect the circuit breaker or power cable before servicing.

steps.title: Drain tub
steps.body: Unit performs 3× 3 min drain on OC. Verify tub not overfilled.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Unit performs 3× 3 min drain on OC. Verify tub not overfilled.

steps.title: Overflow sensor >3 V when tub empty?
steps.body: CN505 pin 1 overflow: OC when ≤3 V for 5 s. Should read >3 V when tub empty after drain.
steps.sourceExcerpt: CN505 pin 1 overflow: OC when ≤3 V for 5 s. Should read >3 V when tub empty after drain.

steps.title: Inlet valve stuck open?
steps.body: Check water valve shuts off; case brake/flow meter not falsely indicating fill (4C5).
steps.sourceExcerpt: Check water valve shuts off; case brake/flow meter not falsely indicating fill (4C5).

steps.title: Replace valve or case brake
steps.body: Replace inlet valve or case brake/flow meter when OC persists with empty tub.

steps.title: Overflow cleared
steps.body: Overflow condition resolved.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Make sure to disconnect the circuit breaker or power cable before servicing.

steps.title: 120 VAC at outlet?
steps.body: Measure voltage at the power outlet. Normal: AC 120 V.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Measure voltage at the power outlet. Normal: AC 120 V.

steps.title: Correct customer power
steps.body: Connect to proper 120 V source or repair outlet wiring.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Connect to proper 120 V source or repair outlet wiring.

steps.title: 120 VAC at CN101?
steps.body: Measure between black and white wires of CN101 on main PBA. Normal: AC 120 V.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Measure between black and white wires of CN101 on main PBA. Normal: AC 120 V.

steps.title: Repair power harness
steps.body: Check and replace power cable or terminal connections to main PBA.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Check and replace power cable or terminal connections to main PBA.

steps.title: 5 VDC present?
steps.body: Measure CN302 pin 4 (orange) to CN301 pin 6 (brown). Normal: 4.5–5.5 V.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Measure CN302 pin 4 (orange) to CN301 pin 6 (brown). Normal: 4.5–5.5 V.

steps.title: 9–12 V rail present?
steps.body: Measure CN301 pin 9 (blue) to pin 11 (blue). Power On: 9.5–12.5 V. Power Off: 5.5–7.0 V.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Measure CN301 pin 9 (blue) to pin 11 (blue). Power On: 9.5–12.5 V. Power Off: 5.5–7.0 V.

steps.title: Replace main PBA
steps.body: Replace main PBA assembly when DC supplies fail after harness repair.

steps.title: Power verified
steps.body: Incoming and on-board DC supplies verified.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Make sure to disconnect the circuit breaker or power cable before servicing.

steps.title: Inspect CN505 thermistor
steps.body: Check CN505 connector seated (pins 5–6 water thermistor). Reconnect if loose.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Check CN505 connector seated (pins 5–6 water thermistor). Reconnect if loose.

steps.title: Thermistor voltage 0.2–4.5 V?
steps.body: With power on, measure voltage across thermistor at CN505. Normal: 0.2–4.5 V.
steps.sourceExcerpt: With power on, measure voltage across thermistor at CN505. Normal: 0.2–4.5 V.

steps.title: Thermistor resistance
steps.body: Power off. Disconnect connector. Measure resistance across thermistor — ~49 kΩ @ 25°C (77°F) per OEM table.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power off. Disconnect connector. Measure resistance across thermistor — ~49 kΩ @ 25°C (77°F) per OEM table.

steps.title: Replace thermistor
steps.body: Replace thermistor or Assy Sensor ECS when out of spec.

steps.title: Thermistor OK
steps.body: Thermistor verified — if tC/HC persists, check heater and main PBA.
